ending: Jake remains on Earth in a guarded recovery after the Malefic Viper repairs his shattered soul. His resource capacity is still reduced, and the corrupted half-core continues its extremely slow absorption inside a permanently sealed skill. Sylphie is alive after cleansing and evacuation, but has lost her right wing. The Fallen King apparently destroys himself and the Desolate Child of Loss in a soul explosion. His records and true soul survive inside the Mask of the Fallen King, although Aaron can find no means of revival. No kill notice confirms the Desolate Child's death, but new planetary desolation has stopped. William finds abnormal connections around the trap without proof that Ell'Hakan directed it. Miranda monitors Ell'Hakan-linked sleepers on Earth while covertly pursuing a separate fanatic network hostile to Jake, outsiders, and beasts. Ell'Hakan's alliance and Earth's coalition continue competing across the unfinished Prima Guardian event. Kindroth remains a useful but independent diplomatic ally, the Risen have a self-governed island settlement, and three beastfolk diplomats have reached Earth. The lunar Ghost Vine Sovereign and Operation Moonfall also remain unresolved.
in_short: Jake Thayne and Sandy discover a B-grade plant-undead fused with the Moon's core, but postpone Operation Moonfall to face the Prima Guardian event. Jake makes Earth's Guardian stronger by choosing an accelerated protocol, then kills it in space and claims Earth's pylon. Earth launches a rival rescue network as Ell'Hakan expands his own alliance. After blackened planets reveal a desolation threat, Jake takes half of a corrupted core into an absorption skill. The experiment nearly destroys his soul, and the Malefic Viper saves him by sealing the skill with the half-core inside. While Jake recovers, Sylphie and the Fallen King are trapped with the Desolate Child of Loss. Sylphie escapes after losing a wing, but the Fallen King stays behind and apparently disperses both himself and the enemy. His true soul remains in his mask. The book ends with Jake recovering, planetary desolation apparently halted, and Earth investigating sleeper agents and independent fanatics tied to Ell'Hakan's influence.

recaps.text: Previously: Jake Thayne is Earth's world leader and the Chosen of the Malefic Viper, though Miranda handles much of the planet's practical administration. Sandy serves as Jake's companion and transport, while Sylphie is his wind-aligned friend and fellow fighter. The Fallen King remains linked to Jake through soul magic, and the Sword Saint stands among Earth's strongest independent combatants. Arnold supports Earth through invention and analysis, while Casper connects Jake's circle to the Risen. Major figures are returning from Nevermore as the planet prepares for the Prima Guardian, a system event that will place Earth and its pylon at risk. Several powerful factions must cooperate despite their conflicting loyalties. Beyond Earth, the god Yip of Yore and his Chosen, Ell'Hakan, remain strategic rivals to Jake and the Malefic Viper. Their competition gives the coming planetary crisis a wider political dimension.

Jake and Sandy travel through subspace to investigate the Moon. Its far side contains the corrupted Lunewood Forest, an artificial ecosystem grown from a system-placed wood meteorite. Sandy descends toward the lunar core while Jake reaches the meteorite, which is dying and tries to take him as a host. Below the surface, Sandy encounters the Ghost Vine Sovereign, a B-grade plant-undead entity fused with the Moon's core. It attacks both explorers, and Sandy's mark disappears, making Jake believe his companion has died. Sandy instead triggers a prepared resurrection and returns through an egg-anchor. The revival saves two stomachs but destroys the others, including Jake's mobile alchemy laboratory, and leaves Sandy severely weakened. The Ghost Vine Sovereign appears largely instinctive and remains bound to the lunar core. Jake and Sandy agree that it must eventually be destroyed even if the Moon cannot be preserved, naming their future plan Operation Moonfall.

Sandy recovers enough to return Jake to Earth before leaving for further treatment. Jake resumes alchemy while Arnold begins rebuilding his Katar and studies the lunar danger. Sylphie helps the Sky Whale bring Earth's strongest beasts under control. Miranda and Lillian return from Nevermore and organize planetary leadership, while Minaga begins combining several rewards into a permanent labyrinth spanning multiple grades. Stormild renews Jake and Sylphie's Union Oath and leaves Jake an unexplained request concerning a mutual acquaintance. Preparations intensify for the Prima Guardian, whose victory would cost Earth its planetary pylon. Ell'Hakan, Yip of Yore's Chosen, leads an alliance of nearly five hundred planets even though his own world can likely survive without it. Casper returns as an envoy for a large Risen population, Jacob seeks entry with a Holy Church group, and Sandy arrives with Vesperia, a Vespernat Hive Queen.

Vesperia reveals herself as a true royal of the Endless Empire with an internal hive, a large drone army, subordinate queens, and elite Queen's Guards. Her authority lets her bring Earth's underground hives into the defense plan without open war. At the World Congress, Jake imposes Earth's rules on hostile visiting factions while Miranda assigns forces for the coming event. Jacob's vision locates the likely desert impact site, and Arnold supplies communications, a legendary void-based Katar, and adaptive armor. William returns early from Nevermore with evidence that Ell'Hakan's homeworld is held by bloodline-reinforced devotion. He believes Ell'Hakan plans to gain influence over world leaders and pylons, but the unknown sponsor behind William's investigation remains unexplained. Earth decides to compete for other worlds after securing itself. Jake leads a compact team of close combatants, ranged attackers, a healer, and other specialists to the confirmed arrival zone while the wider army establishes a perimeter.

Jake enters the arriving vessel alone and accepts an accelerated protocol that immediately frees an enhanced level-349 Exalted Prima Guardian. The strike team attacks as the creature adapts its body to different damage types. Vesperia loses all four Queen's Guards protecting her and restraining the enemy. Arnold contributes an orbital strike, an android decoy, and remote void fire. Maria and Casper are forced out, Aaron is separated, and the Sword Saint, Vesperia, the Fallen King, Carmen, and Caleb suffer severe injuries. William disrupts the orders holding Aaron away, allowing the healer to restore the team. Near defeat, the Guardian copies the Malefic Viper's escape function and flees into space. Jake follows alone, upgrades his wings under the strain, and fights it above Earth. He tears apart most of its remaining body with a concealed arcane attack. The final fragment tries to copy Jake's time-altering ability, fails, ages into ash, and dies. Earth has defeated its Guardian, but Jake is blind, depleted, and waiting in space for Sandy.

The Guardian's death weakens the remaining Primas, allowing Miranda to coordinate Earth's cleanup. Sandy retrieves Jake while he chooses Lone Hunter of Horizon's Edge, committing his class toward solo hunts rather than a permanent party. Once Earth is secure, Jake opens the captured vessel and learns that he ranks first among candidates for the Seat of the Exalted Prima, ahead of Ell'Hakan and an unidentified survivor. Jake claims Earth's planetary pylon, placing its civilization pylons under his authority and granting benefits to the planet's population. The strike-team contributors receive legendary rewards, while Jake receives the still-sealed Seal of the Exalted Prima. The vessel also provides a route into the Alliance teleportation network. Earth begins a wider intervention campaign: Vesperia, Sylphie, and the Fallen King form one group, the Court of Shadows deploys under Caleb, and the Sword Saint and Jake choose separate targets. Miranda, Arnold, and William remain involved in developing broader travel beyond Alliance-controlled destinations.

Earth's hunters begin rescuing other worlds. Vesperia, Sylphie, and the Fallen King clear a weak dwarf-and-ant-hive world and leave its hive in political control. Jake reaches Oleandra's planet after a disastrous early Guardian release has killed most of her elite force. He saves the survivors, kills the Guardian, and warns Oleandra that Ell'Hakan's bloodline can distort emotions. Her world considers cautious contact with Earth. Jake then notices the first fallen planet on the vessel map. On a powerful elven world, he proves his strength while hiding much of it and confronts the leader known as the Voice of the One over exaggerated religious claims. The leader is Kindroth, who ultimately releases the Guardian. Jake kills it with one prepared attack, and Kindroth claims the pylon. Kindroth then becomes Jake's political sponsor, gathering world leaders willing to accept Guardian help without joining Ell'Hakan. Jake gains a list of new destinations, turning individual rescues into a voluntary coalition.

Jake's campaign expands rapidly, and Earth-associated forces clear more than a hundred Guardians. Kindroth organizes access while Miranda evaluates him as an effective but independently motivated ally. A new danger appears when cleared planets turn black on the map, meaning their cores have been destroyed beyond reclamation. During a divided scale-kin world's crisis, Jake avoids a staged confrontation with two leaders aligned to Ell'Hakan. He performs a deliberately misleading melee-only Guardian kill, prompting Yip of Yore to consider recruiting him as a possible usurper of the Malefic Viper or killing him if he refuses. Meanwhile, the Risen receive a self-ruled island on Earth. Arnold's experimental long-range circle lets Jake reach the first blackened world. He finds an airless ruin saturated with desolation and a corrupted planetary core spreading permanent damage. Evidence suggests a limping humanoid entity infused part of its own soul into the core. Jake discovers that his Malefic Viper abilities offer some protection and decides to take a fragment.

Jake tries to remove a small fragment from the corrupted planetary core but breaks it in half. He stores the smaller half inside his absorption skill and escapes to Earth as desolation floods the skill's internal stomach. Aaron keeps him alive while Jake builds a containment structure in his soul space. Jake then applies his primeval origin energy directly to the skill's symbolic representation, triggering an uncontrolled evolution that consumes his soul-space resources and destabilizes his soul. The crisis also injures the Fallen King through their connection. Jake prepares to destroy the skill rather than die, but the Malefic Viper intervenes despite the system's restrictions. He stops the evolution, repairs Jake's shattered soul, and freezes the damaged records. The intervention permanently seals the absorption skill's internal stomach, leaving the half-core trapped inside and only slowly being absorbed. Jake survives with sharply reduced resource capacity and begins a long natural recovery, now owing his patron an even greater debt.

Miranda conceals Jake's condition while Aaron limits his exertion, alchemy, boosting skills, and soul strain. Vesperia returns to protect him, and Sylphie stays until he can defend himself before resuming the wider campaign. The Sword Saint interrupts a civil conflict on a beastfolk world, forces its three kings into negotiations, kills its Guardian, and returns with three diplomats while the political outcome remains unresolved. Ell'Hakan asks Jacob to steer Jake away from the Malefic Viper, while Jacob warns that the conflict between the two Chosen is moving toward one of their deaths. Earth and Ell'Hakan's Holy Church-backed alliance continue competing across the galaxy as desolation consumes more worlds. Sylphie and the Fallen King clear about thirty planets together. On their latest world, its leader kills herself after activating the vessel, trapping them outside its teleportation room. William and Miranda uncover Earth infiltrators linked to that planet and learn their objective is to impose a fate worse than death on Jake. As Sylphie reports the trap, the horizon around her and the Fallen King begins losing color to approaching desolation.

Sylphie and the Fallen King face the Desolate Child of Loss, a living calamity that regenerates massive physical damage and spreads stronger desolation when harmed. Sylphie loses her right wing and amputates it before the contamination can spread. Jake ignores the risk to his damaged soul and travels with Sandy, Aaron, and William to extract them. Aaron cleanses Sylphie, but the Fallen King's desolation is too deeply embedded for Sandy to absorb him in time. He remains behind, transfers his mask into Jake's possession, and burns his soul to hold off the Child while the others escape. The Fallen King attacks the creature's soul and ends in a golden explosion that disperses them both. Jake wakes on Earth after nearly three days. The mask contains the Fallen King's records and true soul, but Aaron finds no reviving spark or restoration method. No kill notice confirms the Desolate Child's death. William can no longer locate its karma and finds abnormal connections to Jake and Ell'Hakan, but no proof that Ell'Hakan knew of or directed the trap.

Earth's investigation separates two hostile networks. Miranda monitors sleeper agents who report to Ell'Hakan but have not yet acted openly. A second, independent fanatic movement targets Jake and the Malefic Viper while recruiting anti-immigrant and anti-beast natives. William cannot reliably identify every member or trace the exact role of bloodline influence, and he refuses direct contact with Ell'Hakan because of the danger to his own stability. Miranda covertly hunts selected threats through her connection to Haven. Elsewhere, Jacob observes that no new planets are becoming desolate and privately infers that Jake's side probably stopped the calamity, though he withholds that conclusion from Ell'Hakan. The Desolate Child's death remains unconfirmed, and the organizer of the trap is still unknown. Jake keeps the Fallen King's true soul safe in the mask and continues his guarded recovery while Earth's coalition and Ell'Hakan's alliance press on with the unfinished Prima Guardian campaign.
